failure_patterns.pattern: endpoint_selection_and_coverage: Agents added irrelevant or redundant calls, or failed to cover distinct requested operations and targets.

rejected_edits.content: For a single broad deliverable, prefer a documented broad or all-scope endpoint when it fully provides the requested output. For explicitly distinct deliverables, check coverage facet by facet and use a direct endpoint for each requested facet when available, even if another endpoint returns overlapping information; include a general-details endpoint when general details are requested in addition to named facets. For each candidate call, identify the requested clause it fulfills and verify the endpoint source and action match. Use only one best-fitting endpoint for a given subject and facet; prune calls justified only by topical association or a broad goal such as a comprehensive overview, and do not call equivalent validators or searches merely to increase confidence. Keep overlapping-provider alternatives only when they provide distinct requested outputs.
rejected_edits.target: For a broad request, prefer a documented broad or all-scope endpoint when it fully provides the requested output; do not choose a narrower endpoint merely because it has fewer required arguments. Conversely, cover separately requested outputs when they require distinct endpoints rather than assuming one broad or multi-capability lookup covers every facet.

rejected_edits.content: Before finalizing, scan optional schema fields for controls needed to express the requested output scope, such as inclusion flags and filters. Set applicable controls and leave unrelated optional fields unset.
rejected_edits.target: If no count is requested, use the smallest conventional value needed.

rejected_edits.content: - **Implement specified behavior for execution requests.** When the user asks to run, test, or compile a program and describes its intended behavior or algorithm without providing source code, call the appropriate execution endpoint and write minimal executable code that implements that description. Use supplied data and only necessary standard or reasonably inferable constants; do not omit the call solely because the source text is absent. Do not fabricate essential inputs that cannot reasonably be inferred.

Also map named sort intent to the exact documented token (for example, “most relevant” to `RELEVANCE` when that enum is listed). Do not omit a requested sort merely because the sort parameter is optional.
rejected_edits.target: If the user explicitly requests default sorting and the endpoint exposes a documented default-sort value, use that value; do not guess or add unrelated parameters.
